The test image shows a corn stalk with numerous brown/tan irregular spots on the lower stem/stalk area. The affected part is the **stem**. 

Stem candidates: Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Common_Smut, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Head_Smut, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Stewart_S_Disease.

The brown spots on the stalk strongly suggest Physoderma_Brown_Spot or Anthracnose. Let me check references one at a time.
Physoderma Brown Spot on stem shows dark purplish-black spots, different from the tan/brown lesions in the test image. Let me check Anthracnose stem.
Anthracnose stem shows shiny black lesions on dried stalks, not matching. Let me check Purple_Leaf_Sheath.
This is a very strong match. Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows tan/brown lesions with dark margins on green stalks, very similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates to be thorough.
Diplodia Stalk Rot shows dried/dead stalks breaking, not matching. Let me check Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, and Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.
Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dark purplish-black spots on the node area, different pattern from the test image. Let me check Charcoal_Stalk_Rot.
Charcoal Stalk Rot shows internal stalk decay with sclerotia, completely different. Let me check Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.
Bacterial Stalk Rot shows water-soaked, mushy tissue with extensive browning, not matching. Let me view a second Purple_Leaf_Sheath reference to confirm the match.

This confirms the match. Both Purple_Leaf_Sheath references show the same pattern as the test image: tan/brown irregular lesions with dark purple-brown margins on green corn stalks, occurring at the leaf collar/sheath area. The setting (field, green growing plants, lower stalk) and lesion appearance (shape, color, location) are nearly identical.
